_meta.purpose: Repository rulesets protecting refs/tags/v* — the tags that cut a production release. Prepared by M29-A, resolved to a real release actor by N-1, and APPLIED on 2026-09-11. This file is the committed description of what is deployed.

applied.not_a_tag_ruleset: 21203909 is `main branch protection (sole owner)` — branch target, unrelated to tags. Recorded in README.md alongside these two so the three are not confused.
applied.first_exercised: Run 34540481139 created v0.0.1-rc3 at b3f5ad64034f9d7123d916a13185009099ddbc0f as Integration#4902397, and Release · Production Gates #47 (run 34540492686) passed on it. The path was proven before creation was locked down, not after.
applied.this_file_is_still_not_evidence: The ids are recorded for humans. Whether GitHub is enforcing any of it is answered only by github.tag_rulesets_active, .tag_ruleset_split, .tag_ruleset_rules, .tag_ruleset_bypass_empty and .tag_ruleset_release_actors, which read GET /rulesets and GET /rulesets/{id} and never read this file.

_meta.why_this_matters: `.github/workflows/release.yml` triggers on `push: tags: ["v*.*.*"]` and every job in it is a mandatory production gate. Until 2026-09-11 tag creation was completely unrestricted, and a production release was one `git push --tags` away with no review, no approval and no required check — demonstrated rather than argued, because v0.0.1-rc1 and v0.0.1-rc2 were both created by an ordinary account with nothing in the way, and either could have been moved or deleted. Both rulesets are now applied: creation on refs/tags/v* is restricted to Integration#4902397, and deletion, non_fast_forward and update are denied to everyone including that App.
_meta.correction_2026_09_10: This block previously said `every job ... ends in building and promoting a container image` and that `GET /rulesets` returned an empty list. Both were stale. release.yml builds two images and promotes NEITHER — both `docker/build-push-action` steps are `push: false`, there is no `docker/login-action` and no registry; the publishing path is `staging-deploy.yml`, which is `workflow_dispatch` and takes a ref as an input. And the list is no longer empty: the `main` ruleset has since been applied. Overstating what the release path can do is the wrong direction of error in the file whose job is to say what is at risk.
_meta.what_this_file_is_not: Evidence. It describes what was applied, which is not the same as showing that GitHub is still enforcing it — a ruleset can be edited or deleted in the UI without this file changing. No check in this repository may read it to decide whether tag protection is live. That question is answered only by `GET /rulesets` plus `GET /rulesets/{id}`, through github.tag_rulesets_active, github.tag_ruleset_split, github.tag_ruleset_rules, github.tag_ruleset_bypass_empty and github.tag_ruleset_release_actors — all of which report EXTERNAL, never PASS, when that live evidence is missing.
_meta.why_two_rulesets: GitHub applies bypass_actors to an entire ruleset, not to individual rules. Restricting *who may create* a release tag requires a `creation` rule plus bypass actors who are exempt from it — and those actors would then also be exempt from every other rule in the same ruleset, including deletion. Splitting the policy keeps tag immutability absolute: the release actors may create tags, and nobody may delete or move one.
_meta.apply_commands_are_historical: These were run on 2026-09-11 and are retained so the rulesets can be recreated from this file, not as a pending instruction. Running them against a repository that already carries these rulesets creates duplicates, which github.tag_ruleset_split catches as more than two active tag rulesets.
_meta.release_actor_resolved: N-1 Path A. rulesets[0].bypass_actors names GitHub App 4902397, "EruoFood Release Governor", installed on this repository only, with Contents: read and write. That is the APP ID — not the installation id, and not the repository owner's user id 36742102. GitHub's ruleset bypass actor types are Integration, OrganizationAdmin, RepositoryRole and Team; there is no User, so a person cannot hold this grant at all and a dedicated App is the only encoding that is both accepted and true. The same actor is recorded in identities.json, and github.tag_ruleset_release_actors compares the two for exact set equality.
unresolved_administrator_inputs: None. The release actor is resolved, both rulesets are applied, and the tag-creation path was exercised before creation was locked down.

Still external, and unrelated to application: that App 4902397 exists and is installed only on this repository. GitHub accepting the id in bypass_actors is now answered — it accepted it on 2026-09-11. Confirm the rest with: gh api /repos/nzebrian/eruofood-ai/installation --jq '{app_id, repository_selection, permissions}'

Standing consequence, not an open input: the repository owner can no longer push a release tag by hand. Only Integration#4902397 can, through .github/workflows/release-tag.yml. If that workflow is ever removed or broken, releases stop — which is why n1_release_tag_control is a mandatory control.
_meta.actor_placeholder_contract: Each entry in rulesets[0].bypass_actors must name a real GitHub actor: {"actor_id": <int>, "actor_type": "Team" | "Integration" | "OrganizationAdmin" | "RepositoryRole", "bypass_mode": "always"}. No wildcard, no RepositoryRole covering all writers, and no `actor_type: "OrganizationAdmin"` used as a shortcut for 'whoever happens to be an admin'. Release authority is a named grant or it is not a grant.
